items.title: Remove legacy --web / --cli compatibility parsing from the dev launcher
items.context: Delete the hidden compatibility branch in packages/main/src/verifier/dev-cli.ts, keep the supported launcher flow unchanged, and make sure the file only reflects the documented surface.
items.userSees: "🐨 lattice serve" followed by "API: http://localhost:<port>" and "Core WS: ws://localhost:<port>"; the launcher starts the documented flow without any special --web / --cli mode.

happy.desc: Running lattice serve with the documented flags still starts the normal core + Dashboard flow; WHY: keeps the supported launcher surface intact.

edge.desc: Running lattice serve --dev="npx vite" or lattice serve --port=N still behaves as before after the alias removal; WHY: preserves the supported launcher options.

adversarial.desc: A grep or smoke fails if --web or --cli reappears in packages/main/src/verifier/dev-cli.ts; WHY: prevents hidden compatibility from returning.

verificationEvidence.command: npm --prefix packages/main run build && npm run test:entrypoints
verificationEvidence.note: dev-cli.ts no longer parses --web/--cli compatibility flags, and the entrypoints smoke now guards that launcher contract end-to-end.
The supported lattice serve flags are still owned by the serve handler and serve implementation, so removing the hidden dev-cli aliases does not remove the documented launcher parameters.
The entrypoints smoke now fails if --web or --cli reappear in packages/main/src/verifier/dev-cli.ts, so the hidden compatibility branch cannot silently return.

items.title: Add a regression check for the launcher contract
items.context: Cover the launcher with a small smoke or unit-style check so the removed flags do not silently return, and keep the documented serve entry points as the only supported ones.
items.userSees: "entrypoints verified" at the end of npm run test:entrypoints; the smoke fails if the legacy serve aliases reappear.

happy.desc: npm run test:entrypoints finishes with entrypoints verified after the launcher change; WHY: proves the root smoke still passes.

edge.desc: The entrypoint check still passes on a clean build with the worktree symlinked node_modules; WHY: keeps the smoke usable in this workspace.

adversarial.desc: The entrypoint smoke fails if the legacy --web / --cli aliases are reintroduced anywhere in the launcher path; WHY: turns the hidden contract back into a guardrail.

verificationEvidence.note: entrypoints smoke now asserts packages/main/src/verifier/dev-cli.ts does not contain hidden --web/--cli compatibility parsing, and the test passes end-to-end.
The entrypoints smoke passes in this worktree after a clean build, so the regression check remains usable in the symlinked node_modules workspace.
The smoke includes a source-level guard on packages/main/src/verifier/dev-cli.ts, so reintroducing --web or --cli makes the test fail.
